## finalfantasy.fandom.com (Information)

- https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Final_Fantasy_Tactics_version_differences -- versions*, platforms* -- accessed 2026-09-22
Mirror: https://breezewiki.com/finalfantasy/wiki/Final_Fantasy_Tactics_version_differences

- https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Final_Fantasy_Tactics -- story, dates*, platforms*, credits, game modes -- accessed 2026-10-18 (page text pasted by user; the mirror https://breezewiki.com/finalfantasy/wiki/Final_Fantasy_Tactics was not in this file before; this is the Final Fantasy Wiki page of the game):
  - Story: set in Ivalice, a unified kingdom of seven territories caught in the War of the Lions between two factions; **Ramza Beoulve, a member of the respected House Beoulve, finds himself caught amid the war and later uncovers the truth behind a sinister plot behind it** (supports the highborn-cadet wording for the description, pending item 3); the first game set in Ivalice, later the setting of Final Fantasy XII and grouped in the Ivalice Alliance series, with the spinoffs Tactics Advance and A2
  - Credits: directed by Yasumi Matsuno, produced by Hironobu Sakaguchi, character designs by Akihiko Yoshida, score by Masaharu Iwata and Hitoshi Sakimoto; the first tactical RPG in the series; developers Squaresoft (PlayStation), Square Enix (The War of the Lions) and Creative Studio III (The Ivalice Chronicles)
  - Release dates: original, PlayStation: Japan June 20, 1997, United States January 28, 1998, Japan again June 29, 2000 (the SMC release); **The War of the Lions: PlayStation Portable Japan May 10, 2007, Europe October 5, 2007, Canada and United States October 9, 2007; PlayStation Network Japan March 9, 2011, Europe June 30, 2011, Canada and United States July 19, 2011; iOS iPhone and iPod Touch United States August 4, 2011, iPad United States February 23, 2012; Android Japan February 14, 2013, United States and Europe June 4, 2015** (the June 4, 2015 date matches the English Play page); The Ivalice Chronicles September 30, 2025 on PlayStation 4 and 5, Switch and Switch 2, PC and Xbox Series X and S; the entry's version years (2007 and 2025, and the 1997 original) agree
  - Game modes: single player, and multiplayer on the PSP only; the entry's tags are only Turn-based tactical RPG, with no Single-player or Multiplayer tag (asked the user, .plan/review-later.md); ratings: ESRB Teen, CERO 12 and up (PlayStation and PSP) and 15 and up (The Ivalice Chronicles), PEGI 12+, USK 12+

## Decisions
- The War of the Lions `apple` row is a plain iOS row with no suffix, linking the US iPhone App Store page (id446760220) (user, 2026-10-17): the iPad version is a separate store entry and "super rare", so no iPad row; a suffix is added only if an iPad icon is ever added; the row's link was the dlgames site before; the iPad and the Japanese store pages are recorded above only
- The War of the Lions version keeps its `…?` and `helpWanted` until its languages are audited (user, 2026-10-18): the smartphone stores show only English and Japanese, but the PSP release likely has European languages, so the PSP edition (and its regional editions) must be checked before the unknown-languages marker is dropped
- The War of the Lions version gained a Japanese Android row (`jpTag`, the FFT_jp2 Play page) beside the English one (user, 2026-10-18: agreed); the English Android edition's release date, Jun 4, 2015 (its Play page), stays in this file only, since the version's date is the 2007 PSP release
- Description rewritten (user, 2026-10-18): "Long after the era of XII, the highborn cadet Ramza is caught in a war between two noble factions and uncovers the sinister plot behind it." with a link to the XII entry; it replaces "Far in the future, the mercenary Ramza is involved in a civil war when an ancient demonic evil starts to take hold over the world": XII is first in both the narrative and chronological orders, so "long after XII" holds in both (Tactics A2 says little about the timeline); the start is Ramza's starting position, the highborn cadet of the en.wikipedia lead (the mercenary step comes later in its plot section); "uncovers the sinister plot" is from the Final Fantasy Wiki; no spoilers (not the murder of Delita's sister, the break with the nobility, Gafgarion's mercenaries or the Lucavi)
